headlines.title: Hacker targets ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ in apparent leak
headlines.description: The gaming world has been rattled by what appears to be a major leak of the highly anticipated “Grand Theft Auto VI,” with the alleged hacker warning other publishers that “no one is safe” from similar breaches.

headlines.title: China’s backflipping robots leap to blockbuster stock market debut in latest sign of AI boom
headlines.description: Unitree’s shares closed up 460% on Wednesday, a significant marker as Beijing competes with Washington for global tech dominance.

headlines.title: Bessent announces new Iranian sanctions in 'Operation Economic Outcast'
headlines.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent held a press conference to announce new sanctions against Iran in a "sustained financial operation" that the Trump administration is calling "Operation Economic Outcast."

headlines.title: Trump threatens to raise auto, truck and metal tariffs on Canada
headlines.description: In a post on social media, President Trump threatened to raise tariffs on Canada for imported cars, trucks, automobile parts and steel after Canadian Prime Minister Carney said he would retaliate economically. NBC News' Gabe Gutierrez reports from the White House on the escalating trade tensions.

headlines.title: Psychiatrist clashes with Clancy attorney on definition of postpartum psychosis
headlines.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial picked up Monday on the cross examination of prosecution rebuttal witness Dr. Avram Mack. NBC News' Steven Romo and legal analyst Misty Marris discuss takeaways from the morning's testimony.

headlines.title: Phone Safety Settings Guide: What to Turn On vs. Keep Off
headlines.description: There are countless safety and privacy settings on our phones and devices so NBC’s business and data correspondent Brian Cheung stops by TODAY to share the best practices for protecting your privacy, including deleting unused apps, turning on multi-factor authentication, shutting off data tracking, and more.

headlines.title: Chinese Humanoid Robots Smash Usain Bolt’s 100-Meter Record
headlines.description: At the World Humanoid Robot Games, a sports competition in China, robots showed they can run faster than humans, with two smashing Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint. The display of technological might is also meant to display feats of science. NBC's Janis Mackey Frayer reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Will People Really Flip Over the New Era of Foldable Phones?
headlines.description: Foldable smartphones are growing in popularity and now Apple is reportedly preparing to launch its own version, so NBC’s Brian Cheung joins TODAY to break down this nostalgic tech trend including the benefits, the downsides, the cost breakdown, and more.

headlines.title: Verb CEO says you should own your data and get paid for it
headlines.description: Companies collect and profit from our personal data every day, but most of that value never makes its way back to consumers. Verb CEO Cyrus Beschloss explains how his company aims to give users control of their information and the ability to earn money from it.

headlines.title: China hosts second Humanoid Robot Games as arms race with U.S. heats up
headlines.description: The second annual World Humanoid Games are set to take place in Beijing. It comes as tension continues to build between China and the U.S. in a technological arms-race. NBC News' Janis Mackey Frayer is there with a preview of some of the up-and-coming robotic talent.

headlines.title: New software helps California schools crack down on staff allegedly viewing explicit content
headlines.description: Child sexual abuse material is spreading online — and showing up on school staff computers. New scanning software in 12 California districts is catching offenders. NBC News' Dana Griffin reports.

headlines.title: New Billy Joel Doc Uses AI Recreation From 1971 Interview
headlines.description: The Piano Man is the subject of a new documentary called “1971: Billy Joel’s Lost Interview.” It’s about a radio interview he did when he was 22 and while the film uses the real interview audio, the video of a young Billy Joel is generated by artificial intelligence. The singer-songwriter is not involved in the project which is set to premiere in September.
